newsitem.title: USA: Tractor Q3 sales helped by hurricane.
newsitem.headline: Tractor Q3 sales helped by hurricane.

text.p: Tractor Supply Co, which operates farm retail stores, said its third quarter sales benefitted from its markdown program and hurricane Fran, as well as its new merchandising program.

The company earlier reported earnings of $2.3 million, or $0.26 per share on sales of $105.0 million, compared to profits of $2.2 million, or $0.25 per share, on net sales of $88.3 million in the period last year.

Tractor also said the company's new fall season merchandising and marketing programs helped sales, and that it is optimistic that these new programs will even more favorably impact the fourth quarter.

Year-to-date through September 28, 1996, it opened 19 new stores, relocated three and reopened its Bowling Green, Ohio store. It plans to open four additional new stores and relocate one additional store during the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996.
Tractor said it expects to open 25 additional new stores in fiscal 1997. It said current plans call for the opening of about 12 new stores in the first quarter of fiscal 1997.

Tractor Supply Company operates 204 retail farm stores in 24 states, offering a selection of merchandise including farm maintenance products, animal products, general maintenance products, lawn and garden products, light truck equipment, and work clothing.
